items.stem: Why will Oedipus not touch Theseus?
options: He believes he is still polluted
He is still too angry with Theseus to greet him
He cannot find Theseus after the fight ends
Theseus forbids any greeting from a guest

items.stem: Who brings the daughters back to Oedipus, according to Antigone?
options: Theseus and his gallant followers
Creon and a band of Theban men
Ismene acting by herself alone
The chorus coming from the grove

items.stem: Complete the line: “My converse somewhat long and _____.”
options: welcome
secret
tedious
bitter

items.stem: Complete the line: “I marvel not if thou hast _____ long”
options: dallied
hurried
knelt
wept

items.stem: Who is the suppliant at Poseidon's altar?
options: Polyneices
Creon
Ismene
A priest of Poseidon

items.stem: What does Theseus say it would be a waste of words to do?
options: Boast of how the fight was won
Ask Oedipus for any further counsel
Swear a new oath after the rescue
Send the daughters back to Creon at once

items.stem: What assurance does Theseus give as he goes out?
options: Oedipus's life is safe while any god saves Theseus
The suppliant will be arrested before he can speak
The daughters must leave Attica before nightfall
Oedipus's resting-place will be shown to every guest

items.stem: Who persuades Oedipus to listen?
options: Antigone
Ismene
The Chorus
Creon

items.stem: How does Oedipus first respond?
options: He refuses to see him
He embraces him at once with joy
He sends him money for the journey
He curses Theseus for bringing the news

items.stem: Complete the line: “Corrupt and _____ with a thousand ills?”
options: honoured
tainted
forgotten
sheltered

items.stem: Complete the line: “I marvel who is this _____.”
options: messenger
captain
stranger
petitioner

items.stem: What does Antigone ask her father to allow?
options: That their brother may come and be heard
That Creon be invited back into the grove
That Theseus hand the daughters over to Argos
That Oedipus leave Attica before the suppliant speaks

items.stem: Why does Theseus tell Oedipus to beware and not fail in due reverence?
options: The man has found asylum at the god's altar
The chorus has already promised the man a crown
The daughters have already sworn to follow him home
The man has brought a Theban army to the shore

items.stem: Who does Antigone say should tell the tale of their ventures, and why?
options: Theseus, from his own lips, so her part may be brief
Ismene, because she saw more of the fight than anyone
The chorus, because only the elders may speak of war
Creon, if he will confess the seizure in public

items.stem: What proof of the oath does Theseus say Oedipus has already had?
options: He has brought the maids back alive and nothing harmed
He has already named the resting-place before the chorus
He has sent Creon home with gifts from Athens
He has promised the daughters a safe escort out of Attica

items.stem: Complete the line: “On my way _____, I fain would have”
options: homeward
skyward
seaward
hitherward

items.stem: Complete the line: “A scheme of villainy is soon _____.”
options: bewrayed
rewarded
forgotten
honoured

items.stem: What tells Oedipus who the suppliant is?
options: Theseus's hint that a kinsman at Argos might claim this boon
A messenger's report that Creon has come back again
The chorus naming the man as a priest of Poseidon
Antigone's claim that Ismene is waiting at the altar

items.stem: When Oedipus yields, what does he beg Theseus to prevent?
options: That anyone should have power to dispose of him
That the daughters be sent ahead to meet the suppliant
That the altar of Poseidon be taken down at once
That Theseus publish the resting-place to every guest

items.stem: How does Theseus treat Oedipus's long converse with the children?
options: He is not jealous and will not take offense at the delay
He rebukes Oedipus for ignoring a king in the grove
He leaves at once and will not hear any later counsel
He demands that the daughters be silent before he speaks

items.stem: Complete the line: “Have thankless children and are _____,”
options: choleric
gentle
silent
weary

items.stem: Complete the line: “They let their savage mood be _____.”
options: rewarded
exorcised
forgotten
praised

items.stem: What is the matter Theseus calls slight, yet worthy of thought?
options: A man of Oedipus's kin has taken sanctuary at Poseidon's altar
A new war has already broken out inside the grove
The daughters have refused to stay in Attica any longer
The chorus has asked to hear the tale of the fight again

items.stem: What lesson does Antigone draw from the past?
options: Of evil passion evil is the end
Revenge is the only duty a father has left
The gods do not care how parents treat their sons
Sons should be refused a hearing in every case

items.stem: Why does Oedipus greet Theseus from where he stands, rather than take his hand?
options: He will not let Theseus touch one fallen to wretchedness and many ills
Theseus has already refused to come within reach of him
The daughters have asked him not to thank the king at all
He means to save his greeting until the suppliant has spoken

items.stem: What is the effect of Theseus reporting the sanctuary before the suppliant is named as a son?
options: The news arrives first as a sacred obligation, and only then as a family blow
The report proves that the altar has already been torn down by force
The speech replaces the reunion with a hidden burial already performed
The king uses the rite to forbid Oedipus from remaining in the land
